[decisions/application/ADR-APP-002-frontend-framework-selection.md#decision-summary]

## Decision Summary

**Standardize on React (with Module Federation for micro-frontends) and Next.js (for shell applications and standalone portals)** as the enterprise frontend framework choices at Gainwell Technologies. React plain builds (Webpack 5) are used for federated remote modules; Next.js is used for authenticated shells and full-stack portals requiring SSR, SSG, or integrated API routes.

---
page_texts.5:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-002-frontend-framework-selection.md#business-context]

### Business Context

Gainwell Technologies operates a portfolio of healthcare SaaS products (Enterprise™, Provider+™, Whole Health™, Connect™, Rx™, Assist™) delivered through a micro-frontend architecture. Multiple teams independently selected frontend frameworks — including Angular, ASP.NET Razor Pages, and various React configurations — resulting in duplicated effort, inconsistent user experience, and friction when composing federated modules across products.

The CTO has requested that the enterprise frontend technology stack be formalized so delivery teams can make consistent, governed implementation decisions without relying on tribal knowledge.
page_texts.6:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-002-frontend-framework-selection.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

The enterprise micro-frontend strategy (documented in the Enterprise Micro-Frontend Architecture white paper) is built on **Webpack 5 Module Federation**. Module Federation imposes constraints on which frameworks and build tools can be used as federated remote modules. The existing portfolio already uses React as the dominant UI library, and teams have accumulated React expertise across engineering squads.

Architecture guidance [GUID-APP-TEC-001](../../strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md) documents the detailed decision criteria for Next.js vs. plain React within this context.
page_texts.7:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-002-frontend-framework-selection.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Without a recorded enterprise decision:

- Teams independently select Angular, Vue, or various React configurations, breaking Module Federation composition
- Shell applications are built as plain React SPAs, missing SSR performance, auth, and SEO capabilities
- Micro-frontend remote modules are built as Next.js applications, conflicting with Module Federation runtime requirements
- Onboarding materials and job descriptions cannot specify a consistent frontend standard
page_texts.8:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-002-frontend-framework-selection.md#decision-drivers]

### Decision Drivers

- 🎯 **Module Federation compatibility**: Remote modules must be consumable by any host shell without framework runtime conflicts
- 🎯 **SSR / Auth / SEO**: Shell applications and full-stack portals need server-side rendering, server-side auth, and SEO support
- 🎯 **Developer experience**: Reduce context-switching cost — one React mental model across both shell and remote module development
- 🎯 **HIPAA compliance**: Server-side session handling and no token exposure in client bundles
- 🎯 **Talent availability**: React has the broadest enterprise engineering talent pool in the healthcare-technology domain
- 🎯 **Bundle budget**: The enterprise ≤500KB gzipped per-module budget eliminates frameworks with heavy runtimes
- ⚠️ **Constraint**: Must not require a full rewrite of existing React-based modules already in production

---
page_texts.9:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-002-frontend-framework-selection.md#required-option]

## Required Option

**Option 1: React (Webpack 5) for federated remote modules + Next.js for shells and standalone applications** ✅ **SELECTED**
page_texts.11:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-002-frontend-framework-selection.md#federated-remote-modules--plain-react-webpack-5]

#### Federated Remote Modules — Plain React (Webpack 5)

Remote modules are independently deployed React applications that expose components and pages via Module Federation. They **must not** use Next.js, as Next.js's custom server and routing layer conflicts with Module Federation host runtime requirements.

- **Build tool**: Webpack 5 with `ModuleFederationPlugin` (see [ADR-APP-004](ADR-APP-004-mfe-platform-layer-selection.md) for platform layer decision)
- **Language**: TypeScript (strict mode, per ADR-APP-001)
- **Component system**: Shadcn/UI + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS (per ADR-APP-003)
- **State management**: Zustand (per GUID-APP-TEC-002)
- **Routing**: React Router v7 (within the remote module's shell boundary)
- **Testing**: Jest + React Testing Library + Playwright (E2E)
- **Accessibility**: WCAG 2.2 AA via Radix UI primitives + axe-core CI validation (per GUID-APP-ACC-001)
page_texts.12:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-002-frontend-framework-selection.md#shell-applications-and-standalone-portals--nextjs-app-router]

#### Shell Applications and Standalone Portals — Next.js (App Router)

Shell applications host and compose multiple federated remote modules. Standalone portals have SEO, SSR, or integrated API route requirements. Both use Next.js.

- **Version**: Next.js 14+ (App Router required; Pages Router is in maintenance mode)
- **Rendering**: SSR for authenticated portal pages; SSG for public marketing/documentation pages
- **Auth**: next-auth (NextAuth.js) for server-side session management; never expose tokens in client bundles
- **Module Federation**: `@module-federation/nextjs-mf` plugin for consuming remote modules
- **API routes**: Next.js Route Handlers (`app/api/`) for BFF (Backend for Frontend) pattern per PTN-APP-API-001
- **Language**: TypeScript (strict mode)
- **Component system**: Shadcn/UI + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS (per ADR-APP-003)
page_texts.13:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-002-frontend-framework-selection.md#migration-path--aspnet-to-react]

#### Migration Path — ASP.NET to React

For teams migrating from ASP.NET Razor Pages, the target stack is determined per the criteria in GUID-APP-TEC-001:

- Migrate to **plain React + Webpack 5** when the application will become a federated remote module
- Migrate to **Next.js** when the application is a top-level portal with auth, SSR, or SEO requirements
page_texts.14:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-002-frontend-framework-selection.md#benefits]

### Benefits

✅ Consistent React mental model shared between shell and remote module development teams
✅ Module Federation composition works without framework runtime conflicts
✅ Next.js delivers HIPAA-compliant server-side auth for authenticated portals
✅ Large open-source ecosystem and strong talent availability
✅ Aligns with GUID-APP-TEC-001 selection guidance already published
✅ Plain React Webpack 5 modules stay within ≤500KB gzipped module budget
page_texts.15:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-002-frontend-framework-selection.md#risks-and-mitigations]

### Risks and Mitigations

⚠️ **Risk**: Teams default to Next.js for remote modules, breaking Module Federation
🛡️ **Mitigation**: GUID-APP-TEC-001 decision tree, enforced at architecture review gate; ADR published as authoritative record

⚠️ **Risk**: Next.js App Router (RSC) is a major shift from Pages Router for teams already on Next.js 12/13
🛡️ **Mitigation**: Pattern library and PTN-APP-MFE-013 migration guidance covers App Router transition; Pages Router modules are not replaced until feature parity achieved

⚠️ **Risk**: Webpack 5 build times increase as module count grows beyond 8 active remote modules
🛡️ **Mitigation**: RSpack migration path preserved (see ADR-APP-004); Nx or `@module-federation/enhanced` adoptable without bundler swap when scale warrants

---
page_texts.17:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-002-frontend-framework-selection.md#option-2-nextjs-for-all-frontend-applications-shell-and-remote]

### Option 2: Next.js for All Frontend Applications (Shell and Remote)

**Description**: Standardize exclusively on Next.js for all applications, including federated remote modules.

**Pros:**
- ✅ Single framework across the entire frontend estate
- ✅ Full-stack capabilities (SSR, SSG, API routes) available everywhere

**Cons:**
- ❌ Next.js custom server and App Router conflict with Module Federation host runtime — modules cannot be reliably federated
- ❌ Forces SSR overhead on remote modules that do not need it, violating the ≤500KB bundle budget
- ❌ Requires complex workarounds (`@module-federation/nextjs-mf` limitations apply to remotes, not just hosts)

**Verdict**: ❌ **Rejected** — Module Federation incompatibility for remote modules is a hard technical constraint

---
page_texts.18:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-002-frontend-framework-selection.md#option-3-angular-for-remote-modules--nextjs-for-shell]

### Option 3: Angular for Remote Modules + Next.js for Shell

**Description**: Use Angular for remote module development (as some teams currently do) and Next.js for shells.

**Pros:**
- ✅ Accommodates existing Angular investment in some teams

**Cons:**
- ❌ Angular runtime (~100KB+ gzipped) conflicts with React runtime in the same Module Federation host — dual-framework bundles exceed budget
- ❌ Breaks shared component system — Angular cannot consume Shadcn/UI (React) components
- ❌ Requires teams to maintain two frontend technology skill sets
- ❌ Doubles onboarding burden for engineers moving between teams

**Verdict**: ❌ **Rejected** — Dual-framework runtime conflict and talent fragmentation outweigh transition cost savings

---
page_texts.19:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-002-frontend-framework-selection.md#option-4-vuejs-for-remote-modules--nextjs-for-shell]

### Option 4: Vue.js for Remote Modules + Next.js for Shell

**Description**: Allow Vue.js as an alternative remote module framework.

**Pros:**
- ✅ Vue.js is lightweight and developer-friendly

**Cons:**
- ❌ Same dual-runtime conflict as Angular — Vue runtime alongside React adds bundle overhead
- ❌ Vue cannot consume React (Radix UI / Shadcn) component primitives
- ❌ No existing Vue expertise in current Gainwell engineering teams

**Verdict**: ❌ **Rejected** — No existing skill base; dual-runtime conflict; design system incompatibility

---
page_texts.20:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-002-frontend-framework-selection.md#decision-outcome]

## Decision Outcome

**Selected Option**: **Option 1 — React (Webpack 5) for federated remote modules + Next.js for shell applications and standalone portals**
page_texts.21:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-002-frontend-framework-selection.md#justification]

### Justification

The enterprise micro-frontend strategy is built on Module Federation, which imposes a hard constraint that remote modules cannot use Next.js without significant workarounds. React with Webpack 5 is the only framework that satisfies both Module Federation composition and the ≤500KB per-module budget simultaneously.

Next.js is the right choice for shell applications and standalone portals because its SSR, auth, and API route capabilities address the HIPAA session management requirement without additional infrastructure.

The combination results in a single React mental model across shell and remote development, maximizing talent portability.
page_texts.23:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-002-frontend-framework-selection.md#positive-outcomes-]

#### Positive Outcomes ✅

- Teams can compose micro-frontends without framework runtime conflicts
- HIPAA-compliant server-side auth delivered via Next.js shells
- Single React skill set required across all frontend teams
- Module Federation host/remote composition pattern is officially standardized
- Accelerated onboarding: one frontend standard to learn
page_texts.24:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-002-frontend-framework-selection.md#negative-outcomes-]

#### Negative Outcomes ⚠️

- Teams with existing Next.js remote modules must migrate to plain React + Webpack 5 (migration window to be defined per team roadmap)
- Angular-based teams require cross-training investment (coordinated via talent development plan)
- Webpack 5 build performance at scale (>8 active modules) requires RSpack migration or Nx adoption per ADR-APP-004 re-evaluation criteria
page_texts.25:
[decisions/application/ADR-APP-002-frontend-framework-selection.md#neutral-outcomes-ℹ]

#### Neutral Outcomes ℹ️

- Decision does not affect backend technology selections (C#/.NET, Java, Python, Node.js remain governed by ADR-APP-001)
- React Native is out of scope; mobile framework selection is a separate decision
